title: Drivers of Water Resource Changes Over the Mediterranean Climate Regions of the Northern Hemisphere
content:
Abstract

Mediterranean Climate Regions (MCRs) are water-limited areas highly sensitive to global warming and hydroclimatic change. However, long-term declines and interannual variability in water availability, as well as their climate drivers, remain poorly understood. This study exploits the GRACE/GRACE-FO satellite observations of Total Water Storage (TWS) spanning 2002–2023 to investigate TWS variability and its drivers in the Euro-Mediterranean (Euromed) and the Western United States (WUS) MCRs. We apply a multiple linear regression (MLR) model on temperature, total precipitation and two metrics capturing complementary precipitation features: Intensity (above 95th Percentile; IPA95P) and Intermittency of storms above 5 mm (MDDA5). The MLR model explains 64% of observed TWS variability across Northern Hemisphere MCRs. While temperature and precipitation are the primary drivers of the explained TWS variance (contributing to 37% and 36%, respectively), IPA95P and MDDA5 explain a smaller yet non-negligible fraction (up to 15%), with their effects concentrated in specific regions. Precipitation primarily drives interannual TWS variability, whereas increasing temperature governs the long-term decline. Temperature-driven TWS loss rates reach up to −1.2 mm/year in Euromed and −0.9 mm/year in WUS, corresponding to TWS sensitivities per degree of warming of up to −25 mm/°C in North Africa, −34 mm/°C in East Euromed and −36 mm/°C in South WUS. Under the intermediate SSP2-4.5 scenario, projected TWS declines by 2100 reach −60 mm in North Africa, −84 mm in East Euromed, and −94 mm in South WUS relative to the 1995–2014. These results reveal critical vulnerabilities in MCRs, where warming-induced drying may exacerbate transitions toward a more arid climate.
